PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Functions - Recursion

Recursion

Every recursive problem can be divided into a base case and a recursive case.

•  Base Case: This is the simplest subproblem the problem can be reduced to. In a
   recursive solution, the base case is the one case you know the direct solution
    for.

•  Recursive Case: Any case that isn’t the base case is automatically a recursive
   case. We don’t know the solutions for these cases; instead, we split them
   further into simpler cases until we reach the base case.

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Functions - Recursion

Recursion – Basic Example

Take the example of opening a set of Russian nesting dolls.

Base Case: The doll doesn’t open. This means we’ve reached the
smallest  doll, and  represents  the  stopping  condition  for  our
recursion.

Recursive Case: The doll opens. This means we still haven’t finished
opening the set, and we need to perform some action here called the
recursive step.

Recursive Step: If you have a doll that can open (i.e., recursive case),
then open it and see if the doll inside it can open. This is the action
we perform on the recursive case to get it closer to the base case.

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Functions - Recursion

Recursion – Basic Example

We can illustrate this using pseudocode as follows:

function OpenDoll(doll):

    # Recursive Case

        OpenDoll(smaller_doll_inside)   # Recursive Step

# Start the recursive process by opening the largest doll
OpenDoll(largest_doll)

Need for Recursion

•  Used to simplify complex problems into smaller, easier problems
•  Solving problems with repeated patterns
•  Handling unknown levels of depth (number of steps to a problem)
•  Mathematical and algorithmic problems

Criteria for Implementing Recursion

•  Recursive functions must have a base case or stopping condition
•  Every recursive call to the function must take a step towards reaching
   the base case

Implementation of Recursion

•  Recursion is implemented using stack because activation records are
   to be stored in LIFO order (last in first out).
• An activation record of a function call contains arguments,g            , return
   address and local variables of the function.
•  Stack is a linear data structure in which elements are inserted to the
   top and deleted from the top.

Stack Memory Allocation
•  In Python, function calls and the references are stored in stack memory.
•  Allocation happens on contiguous blocks of memory – referred as Function call Stack.
•  The size of memory to be allocated is known to the compiler and whenever a function
    is called, its variables get memory allocated on the stack.
•  Any local memory assignments such as variable initializations inside the particular
   functions are stored temporarily on the function call stack, where it is deleted once
   the function returns.
•  This allocation onto a contiguous block of memory is handled by the compiler using
   predefined routines.

Callback Functions
• A callback function is a function that is passed to another function as an
  argument.

def process_data(data, callback):

    callback(result)      # Call the callback function with the result

def print_result(result):

data = [1, 2, 3]
process_data(data, print_result)

Filter() Function

•Filter function filters the given sequence with the help of a function that tests each
element in the sequence to be true or not.

•There are cases where we want to remove a few elements of the input iterable.
ThenThen wewe makemake useuse ofof thethe filterfilter functionfunction.

•Syntax: filter(function, sequence/iterable)
•function: function that tests if each element of a sequence is true or not.

•sequence: The sequence which needs to be filtered, it can be sets, lists, tuples, or
containers of any iterators.


                                                                                                                                          1•Returns: an iterator that is already filtered.

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Filter() Function


The filter function has the following characteristics.

•  Input : an iterable of some number of elements (say n)

•  Output: a lazy iterable of 0 to n elements (between 0 and n)

•  Elements in the output: apply the callback on each element of the
     iterable – if the function returns true, then the input element is
    selected otherwise the input element is rejected.

 Functions - Closure


A closure is a nested function which has access to a free variable from an enclosing
function that has finished its execution.

Three characteristics of a Python closure are:
•  It is a nested function
•  It has access to a free variable in outer scope
•  It is returned from the enclosing function

A free variable - a variable that is not bound in the local scope.

Closures with immutable variables such as numbers and strings - use the nonlocal keyword.

Functions - Decorators



• A powerful and useful tool in Python since  it allows programmers to modify the
   behavior of function or class.


•  Decorators wrap a function and modify its behavior in one or the other way, without
  changing the source code of the function being decorated.


•  In Decorators, functions are taken as the argument into another function and then
   called inside the wrapper function.

 Function Decorators are used


• WhenWhen wewe needneed toto changechange thethe behaviorbehavior ofof aa functionfunction withoutwithout modifyingmodifying thethe functionfunction
    itself.
   Eg: logging, test performance, verify permissions and so on.


• When we need to run the same code on multiple functions. This avoids writing
   duplicate code.

1. Example:
def func_decorator(func):
  def inner_func():
      print("Hello, before the function is called")

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
 Functions - Generators


•  A generator is a function that returns an iterator that produces a sequence of values
  when iterated over.

•  Iterator - an object that can be iterated upon, i.e. we can traverse through all the values.

•  Generators in Python provides a way to create a function that behaves like an iterator.

•  Does not return a single value; instead, it returns an iterator object with a sequence of
   values.

• A yield statement is used instead of the return statement.

•   If the body of a def contains yield, the function automatically becomes a Python
   generator function.

• When the generator function  is called,  it does not execute the function body
   immediately. Instead,  it returns a generator object that can be iterated over to
  produce the values.

Generator Object


•  Python Generator functions return a generator object that is iterable (used as

    •  using the generator object in a “for” loop (Refer Example 1)

Multiple generators can be used to pipeline a series of operations

re Module

The re module in Python provides support for Regular Expressions (regex). Regex is a powerful text-processing tool used to search, match, and manipulate patterns in strings. Helps automate tasks like validation, extraction, text cleaning, and pattern matching. Need not use pip install, as it is a built-in (standard library) module in Python.
A pattern defines what you want to search in text
Examples:
r"\d+" → any sequence of digitsr"\b[Pp]\w+" → words starting with P or pr"\w{3}" → exactly 3 characters
Why not use string methods?
.find() searches exact text
RegEx can match flexible patterns

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Key Metacharacters

Meta | Meaning | Example

. | Any character (except newline) | h.t → hat, hot

\d | Digit (0–9) | \d\d → 12

\w | Word character (a-z, A-Z, 0-9, _) | \w\w → hi, A5

\s | Whitespace | hello\sworld → hello world

+ | One or more | \d+ → 123

* | Zero or more | ab*c → ac, abc

[] | Character set | [aeiou] → any vowel

^ | Start of string | ^Hello

$ | End of string | world$

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Main Functions in re

re.search() → finds first match
re.findall() → finds all matches in a list

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

re.search() Example

import re
text = "My car brand is Audi."
pattern = r"c\w\w"  # 3-letter word starting with 'c'
match = re.search(pattern, text)
if match:
    print(match.group(), match.start(), match.end())
Output:
car 3 6
.group() → actual text.start() → starting index.end() → ending index

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

re.findall() Examples

text = "My numbers: 123, 456, 789."
print(re.findall(r"\d", text))      # single digits → ['1','2',...]
print(re.findall(r"\d+", text))     # full numbers → ['123','456','789']
print(re.findall(r"\w+", "Python is fun!"))  # words → ['Python','is','fun']

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

re.sub() Example

Replace spaces with underscores
import re
text = "Welcome to Python class"
new_text = re.sub(r"\s", "_", text)
print(new_text)

Output:
Welcome_to_Python_class
re.sub(pattern, replacement, text) → substitute function

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Word Boundaries & Quantifiers

\b → word boundary
{n} → exactly n characters
Examples:
text = "The fox ran"
print(re.findall(r"\b\w{3}\b", text))  # ['The','fox','ran']
print(re.findall(r"\w+ing", "learning coding swimming"))  # ['learning','coding','swimming']

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Splitting and Replacing

Splitting

text = "apple, banana orange,grapes"
print(re.split(r"[\s,]+", text))  # split by spaces or commas
Output: ['apple','banana','orange','grapes']

Replacing
text = "Password: 12345"
print(re.sub(r"\d","*",text))  # replace digits → Password: *****

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Matching Patterns

Words starting with p or P:
text = "Python programming is popular"
pattern = r"\b[Pp]\w+"
print(re.findall(pattern, text))  # ['Python','programming','popular']

Text starting with "Hello":
text = "Hello world"
pattern = r"^Hello"
if re.search(pattern, text): print("Starts with Hello")

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Emails & Phone Numbers

Find emails:text = "info@pes.edu, support@pes.com"

# ['info@pes.edu','support@pes.com']

Find 10-digit numbers:

transcript_segments.text: Hello everyone and welcome. Today we are going to explore Pillow, the modern version of Python Imaging Library, also called PIL.
Simple and powerful library that helps us open images, edit images, and save images in multiple formats.
It specially deals with image processing tasks. Let's begin.

Pillow is widely used because it is easy to understand, support many image formats, and includes built-in functions for tasks like resizing, cropping, rotating and filtering images. To install Pillow module, we simply use Pip install pillow.
To start with below, we first import the image class. So image is a class here. Here's a basic code to open an image and display it on the screen.
So for that, image class open function lets you to open the image that is there in the argument. Image.show displays it using your system's default viewer.
Pillow supports JPEG, PNG, BMP, JIF, TIF, and many more image formats. So this example is importing the image class and using the functions open and show.
Once we load the image, we can check some important details like format, which tells the file type like JPEG, or GIF, or Tiv, etc. Then the size, which gives the width and height in pixels.
Then the mode shows the colour representation such as RGB or grayscale.
These properties help us understand the image before processing it.
Resizing is one of the most common operations in image processing. Here's how we resize an image.
So this resize function resizes the image to a given dimension. But it may distort the aspect ratio.
To maintain the aspect ratio we can use thumbnail. This ensures the image is resized without stretching or squashing.
converting the image modes. You can use convert function
to convert to an image to a different colour mode. The common colour modes are one, which is pure black and white, it's just one bit. So zero stands for black, one stands for white.
L, which is grayscale. All the shades of gray colour will be represented in an 8-bit representation. Then RGB, red, green, blue colour, three channels, and this is also an 8-bit representation.
RGBA.
Red, green, blue, and A stands for alpha, which is represents the transparency. Then C M Y K, which stands for Syan, Majenta, Low, and Black.
Mostly used in printing.
Mode conversion is especially useful in machine learning preprocessing, where special formats are required.

Next one, let's take a look into few more essential operations like saving images. To save an image that you have worked on, you can use save function. Then to rotate an image, you can use rotate function and give the degrees as argument.
To crop an image, we can use crop function and the syntaxes you can give the pixel coordinates as left, upper, right, lower to extract the specific region from the image.
These operations make Pillow extremely useful for automation workflows, image editing tasks, and pre processing pipelines.

Thank you. To summarize, Pillow is a very powerful and big enough friendly Python library for image processing. We learned how to use open images, display them, resize, convert color modes, rotate, crop and save images.
With these foundations you can build a wide variety of image based applications from simple editors to machine learning pipelines. Thank you for watching and happy coding.

Recursion

•  There are many problems for which the solution can be
   expressed in terms of the problem itself.

•  The problem is solved by breaking it down into simpler                                                                                      FunctionFunction AA
   versions of itself and working on those, until you get to a
   “base case” or stopping point.                                                                 ………………………..
                                                         …………………………

Functions - Recursion

Recursion

Every recursive problem can be divided into a base case and a recursive case.

•  Base Case: This is the simplest subproblem the problem can be reduced to. In a
   recursive solution, the base case is the one case you know the direct solution
    for.

•  Recursive Case: Any case that isn’t the base case is automatically a recursive
   case. We don’t know the solutions for these cases; instead, we split them
   further into simpler cases until we reach the base case.

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Functions - Recursion

Recursion – Basic Example

Take the example of opening a set of Russian nesting dolls.

Base Case: The doll doesn’t open. This means we’ve reached the
smallest  doll, and  represents  the  stopping  condition  for  our
recursion.

Recursive Case: The doll opens. This means we still haven’t finished
opening the set, and we need to perform some action here called the
recursive step.

Recursive Step: If you have a doll that can open (i.e., recursive case),
then open it and see if the doll inside it can open. This is the action
we perform on the recursive case to get it closer to the base case.

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Functions - Recursion

Recursion – Basic Example

We can illustrate this using pseudocode as follows:

function OpenDoll(doll):
    # Base Case
    ifif ddollll iis ththe smallestll  t ddoll:ll
        print("This is the smallest doll. Stop opening.")
    # Recursive Case
    else:
        print("Opening doll to find a smaller one inside.")
        OpenDoll(smaller_doll_inside)   # Recursive Step

# Start the recursive process by opening the largest doll
OpenDoll(largest_doll)

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Functions - Recursion

Need for Recursion

•  Used to simplify complex problems into smaller, easier problems
•  Solving problems with repeated patterns
•  Handling unknown levels of depth (number of steps to a problem)
•  Mathematical and algorithmic problems

Criteria for Implementing Recursion

•  Recursive functions must have a base case or stopping condition
•  Every recursive call to the function must take a step towards reaching
   the base case

Example: Computation of factorial of a number

factorial(0)=1

factorial(2)=2*1

                                                                     n*factorial(n-1)      otherwise.
.
.
factorial(n)=n*(n-1)*(n-2)*……………….*1


 factorial(n)=n *  factorial(n-1)

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Functions - Recursion

Implementation of Recursion

•  Recursion is implemented using stack because activation records are
   to be stored in LIFO order (last in first out).
• An activation record of a function call contains arguments,g            , return
   address and local variables of the function.
•  Stack is a linear data structure in which elements are inserted to the
   top and deleted from the top.

Implementation of Recursion

•  Consider the example of computing the factorial of a number.

def fact(n): #Recursive Function
            ifif nn ==== 00 :: #terminating#terminating conditioncondition
               res = 1
        else:
               res = n * fact(n - 1)
        return res

•  Suppose we want to compute fact(3). The above function gets executed
   using a stack.

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Functions - Recursion


                                         • When the function call is made recursively,
                                   the activation record for each call will be
                                   placed on the top of the stack.

                                             calls fact(2), fact(1) and fact(0); the
                                        activation record for each of these calls gets
                                     inserted to top of the stack.

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

                                      Condition), the function call stops and
                                          fact(0) is popped out from the top of
                                   the stack.
                                         •   It returns 1, then the recursion
                                     backtracks and solves the pending
                                     function calls. These are popped out of
                                   the stack as they get computed.

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Stack Memory Allocation
•  In Python, function calls and the references are stored in stack memory.
•  Allocation happens on contiguous blocks of memory – referred as Function call Stack.
•  The size of memory to be allocated is known to the compiler and whenever a function
    is called, its variables get memory allocated on the stack.
•  Any local memory assignments such as variable initializations inside the particular
   functions are stored temporarily on the function call stack, where it is deleted once
   the function returns.
•  This allocation onto a contiguous block of memory is handled by the compiler using
   predefined routines.

           if n == 0 : #terminating condition

Fibonacci Series\n"))                                              3

                                                                     Output:

                                                                           Enter number
   print ("Move disk",n,"from source",src,"to destination",dest)                                                                              of disks 3
  TowerOfHanoi(n-1, aux, src, dest)                          Move disk 1 from source A to destination C
                                                        Move disk 2 from source A to destination B

                                                        Move disk 3 from source A to destination CTowerOfHanoi(n,'A','B','C')                                                        Move disk 1 from source B to destination A
                                                        Move disk 2 from source B to destination C
                                                        Move disk 1 from source A to destination C

Functions - Recursion

Example 5 – To add two numbers using recursion

def add(x, y): #Recursive Function
   if(y == 0):  #terminating condition
    return x
  return add(x,dd(  y - 1)) + 1

print("Sum =", add(10, 20))

Output:
Sum = 30

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Functions - Recursion

Example 6 – To subtract two numbers using recursion

def subtract(x, y): #Recursive Function
   if(y == 0):      #terminating condition
    return x
  return subtract(x-1,b      (    y-1))

print("Result =", subtract(10, 20))

Output:
Result = -10

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Functions - Recursion

Example 8 – To divide two numbers using recursion

def divide(x, y):  #Recursive Function
   if(x < y):       #terminating condition
    return 0
  else:l
     return 1 + divide(x - y, y)

print("Result:", divide(20, 5))

Output:
Result: 4

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
 Functions - Recursion

 Recursion vs. Iteration

             Recursion                       Iteration
                  Function calls itself                       Set of program statements executed
                                                           repeatedly
                ImplementedImplemented usingusing FunctionFunction callscalls         ImplementedImplemented usingusing LoopsLoops
                  Termination condition is defined within    Termination condition is defined in the
                 the recursive function                       definition of the loop
                 Leads to infinite recursion, if does not      Leads to infinite loop, if the condition in
               meet termination condition               the loop never becomes false
                           It is slower than iteration                          It is faster than recursion
                Uses more memory than iteration        Uses less memory compared to recursion

Note: When a problem can be solved both recursively and iteratively with similar programming effort, it is generally
best to use an iterative approach.

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
 Functional Programming

• Functional programming  is a programming paradigm where programs are
  constructed by applying and composing functions.
• It    is basically a study of computations with functions which uses pure
  functions, recursive functions, nested functions ,lambda functions etc.
• The ability of functional programming languages to treat functions as values
 and pass them to functions as parameters make the code more readable and
  easily understandable.
• They depend only on the input given to them, and the output will be the
  return value. Their function signature gives all the information about them i.e.
  their arguments and return type etc.



                                                                                                                                          1

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
 Functional Programming

• Higher order  functions are the  functions  that  take other  functions  as
 arguments and they can also return functions. (Ex: Callback Functions)
• They are deterministic in nature .
• TheyThey cancan bebe understoodunderstood veryvery easilyeasily asas theythey don’tdon t changechange statesstates ofof anyany
  variables.
• Testing and debugging is easier. They use immutable values
• Offers better modularity with a shorter code
• Increased productivity of the developer
• It adopts lazy evaluation which avoids repeated evaluation because the value
  is evaluated and stored only when it is needed.
• Example: Functional Constructs like Lazy Map & Lists ,tuples, sets etc.                         2

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
The keyword - lambda

Lambda (Anonymous function/Nameless Function/ Throw away function creation)

• Lambda functions are functions without the name.
• ItIts alsol   calledll d as anonymous ffunctionsti    or ththrow away ffunctions.ti
• It can have any number of arguments but can have only one expression.
• The expression is executed and returned (Implicit return)
• Lambda functions are used when function objects are required.
• Lambda functions are used when you need a particular function for a short
  period of time.


                                                                                                                                          3

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
The keyword - lambda


 Advantages:

 •Lambda functions in Python are very useful in defining the in-line functions.

 •Most suitable when it is used as a part of another function(especially with map,
  filter and reduce functions)

  •Less Code (Concise code)





                                                                                                                                          4

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
The keyword - lambda

 Syntax: lambda input arguments: expression / Output


  •  lambda is a keyword used to declare lambda function.
  •  Input arguments: It can have multiple arguments (if there are more than
    one arguments, then separate the arguments by a comma).
  •  Expression or output: Expression gets evaluated and results are returned





                                                                                                                                          5

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Examples

Example1: To find the square of a number (Comparison between
normal and lambda function)

          Normal Function          Lambda Function

       def square(n):            square=lambda n : n*n
          return n*n

        print(square(4))             print(square(4)) #Function Call





                                                                                                                                          6

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
 Examples

Example 2: To find the greatest of two numbers using the relational
operator.


 maximum=lambdal  bd  a,bb : a iff a>bb elsel  bb  #max(a,b)(  b) can alsol  bbe usedd
 print("The maximum is ",maximum(6,7))
 print(maximum,type(maximum))

 Output:
 The maximum is 7
 <function <lambda> at 0x00000217A6F93550> <class 'function'>


                                                                                                                                            7

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Examples

The power of lambda is better understood when you use them as an anonymous
                                         •
function inside another function.

Example 3
Suppose we have a function definition that takes one argument, and that
argument will be multiplied with an unknown number.
def myfunc(n):
     return lambda a : a * n

double_N = myfunc(2)

print(double_N(12))              Output:24
                                                                                                                                          8

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Examples

We can use the same function definition to make two functions (doube_N and triple_N
functions) in the same program.    •

Example 4
def myfunc(n):y      (  )
   return lambda a : a * n

double_N = myfunc(2)
triple_N = myfunc(3)                Output
                                30
print(double_N(15))                45
print(triple_N(15))


                                                                                                                                          9

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Map() Function


Python map() function is a built in function which  is utilized to apply a function to each
element of an iterable (like a list or a tuple) and returns a new iterable object.

 Syntax: map(function, iterables)

1. The map() function takes two arguments: a function and iterables.
2. The  first argument for the map function  should be a callable which takes one
   argument – could be a free function, function of a type, user defined function, or a
   lambda function.
3.  This function  will be applied to every element of the iterable, and creates a map
    object which is also an iterable.



                                                                                                                                         10

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Map() Function

Working:

•  The map function causes iteration through the iterable, and applies the callable
   on each element of the iterable

•   All these happen only conceptually as the map function is lazy and the above
   said operations happen only after the map object is iterated.

•  We can force an iteration of the map object by passing the map object as an
   argument for the list or set constructor.

•  We can pass one or more iterable to the map() function.

                                                                                                                                         11

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Map() Function

Lazy and Eager objects:
Under lazy object creation, the object  is created when it is needed whereas in the case of
eager object creation,  an object  is created as soon  it  is instantiated. A lazy object
representing a function would be quick to create, and  populate itself with information
when that information is requested. Built-in functions like range(),map(),zip() and open()
functions are basically lazy function objects.

Example:
As map object can be iterated over, the computation will be done for only one item in each
loop. In contrast, when we use list, which is an eager object, it  basically computes all the
values at one time.

Lazy evaluation can be a powerful technique for optimizing code and improving
performance, but it is only sometimes necessary or appropriate.                                   12

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Map() Function

Choosing between lazy and eager evaluation
• When deciding which evaluation strategy to use for a given programming problem,
   there is no one-size-fits-all answer. The choice depends on the nature of the problem,
   the characteristics of the data, the requirements of the solution, and the preferences
   of the programmer.
•  However, some general guidelines can be followed to help make an informed
   decision. For instance, lazy evaluation should be used when you want to delay or
   avoid computations that are not needed, save memory by avoiding intermediate
   results, create and manipulate  infinite or recursive data structures, or explore
   multiple possibilities without committing to one.
• On the other hand, eager evaluation  is preferable when you want to perform
   computations as soon as possible, exploit parallelism or concurrency, or ensure
   predictable and consistent performance.

                                                                                                                                         13

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Map() Function


Example 1 To double all numbers using map and lambda

numbers = (1, 2, 3, 4)
result = map(lambda x: x + x, numbers)
print(list(result))

Output:

<class 'map'>
[2, 4, 6, 8]




                                                                                                                                         14

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Map() Function

Example 2 – To add two lists using map and lambda

num1 = [4, 2, 5]
num2 = [6, 8, 9]

result = map(lambda x, y: x + y, num1, num2)
print(list(result))

Output:
[10, 10, 14]





                                                                                                                                         15

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Map() Function

Example 3 – Function that doubles even numbers present in the list.
def double_num(n):
   if n% 2 == 0:
    return n * 2
  else:
    return n

numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

# Use map to apply the function to each element in the list
result = list(map(double_num, numbers))
 print("The modified list is ",result)

Output: The modified list is [1, 4, 3, 8, 5]                                                                       16

•function: function that tests if each element of a sequence is true or not.

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Filter() Function


The filter function has the following characteristics.

•  Input : an iterable of some number of elements (say n)

•  Output: a lazy iterable of 0 to n elements (between 0 and n)

•  Elements in the output: apply the callback on each element of the
     iterable – if the function returns true, then the input element is
    selected otherwise the input element is rejected.

marks = [55, 78, 90, 87, 65, 45]

  if m <70 :
  return False
 else:
  return True

Distinction = list(filter(myFunc, marks))
print("Students with marks greater than 70 are",Distinction)

Output:
Students with marks greater than 70 are [78, 90, 87]                                                       3

Example 2: Function that filters vowels
def fun(char):
   letters = ['a', 'e', 'i', 'o', 'u']
   if (char in letters):
    return True
  else:
    return False

characters = ['h', 'e', 'l', 'l', 'o', 'w', 'o', 'r','l','d']

                                                                                                                                          5The even number list is [0, 2, 8]

using Lambda function in filter function

  return num % 3 == 0

# Create a list of numbers to filter

Output:
The list of multiples of 3 is [3, 6, 9]


                                                                                                                                          6

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Examples

and Lambda function.

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
reduce() Function
Introduction

The reduce() is a  function that applies a given function to the elements of an iterable,
reducing them to a single value. This function is defined in “functools” module.
Syntax
functools.reduce(function, iterable[, initializer])

•  The function argument is a function that takes two arguments and returns a single
   value. The first argument is the accumulated value, and the second argument is the
   current value from the iterable.
•  The iterable argument is the sequence of values to be reduced.
•  The optional initializer argument is used to provide an initial value. If no initializer is
   specified, the first element of the iterable is used as the initial value.

                                                                                                                                          1

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
reduce() Function

Working of reduce function:

•At first step, first two elements of the sequence are picked and the result is
obtained.
•The•The samesame functionfunction isis appliedapplied toto thethe previouslypreviously attainedattained resultresult andand thethe numbernumber justjust
succeeding the second element and the result is again stored.
•This process continues till no more elements are left in the container.
•There will be n – 1 calls if no initializer is specified.(n is the number of elements in
the input iterable)
•The final result is returned as a single value.





                                                                                                                                          9

  •  Python  zip() method takes iterable containers and returns a  single

    be used just using a single entity.
  •  The function zip is used to associate the corresponding elements of two
    or more iterables into a single lazy iterable of tuples.
  •    It does not have any callback function.

  •  The  resulting  iterable contains  tuples, where the  first

    element from each list is paired together, and so on.

Python For Computational Problem Solving
max() and min() Functions in Python


 Python provides built-in functions to find the largest and smallest values among a
             set of numbers — no loops or manual comparisons needed.

      max()              min()


       •   Returns the largest value                                  •   Returns the smallest value

       •   Works with lists, tuples, sets                              •   Works with lists, tuples, sets

       •   Takes multiple values directly                             •   Takes multiple values directly

       •   Great for finding the top score or                        •   Great for finding the lowest score or
          price                                                       price

Python For Computational Problem Solving
max() Function – Introduction


 •  max() is a built-in Python function.
 •   It returns the largest value among the        Syntax
    given values.                                        max(iterable)
 •   It can also be used with collections
                                        max(value1, value2,
    such as lists, tuples and sets.                                             value3, ...)
 •  Works with numbers and strings
     (alphabetical order).
 •  On a tie, it returns the first maximum
    found.

Python For Computational Problem Solving
max() Function – Example




    Code
    numbers = [10, 25, 15, 40, 5]
    print(max(numbers))





                                Output

                  40



           max() scans every element in the list and returns 40, since it is greater than all the rest.

Python For Computational Problem Solving
min() Function – Introduction


 •  min() is a built-in Python function.
 •   It returns the smallest value among the       Syntax
    given values.                                        min(iterable)
 •   It can be used with lists, tuples, sets
                                        min(value1, value2,
   and other iterables.                                             value3, ...)
 •  Works with numbers and strings
    (alphabetical order).
 •  On a tie, it returns the first minimum
    found.

Python For Computational Problem Solving
min() Function – Example



     Code
    numbers = [10, 25, 15, 40, 5]
    print(min(numbers))





                                Output

                   5



              min() scans every element in the list and returns 5, since it is smaller than all the rest.

Python For Computational Problem Solving
Using max() and min() Together



   Code
   numbers = [12, 45, 7, 23, 56, 9]
   largest = max(numbers)
   smallest = min(numbers)
   print("Largest:", largest)
   print("Smallest:", smallest)





                  Largest: 56    Smallest: 7




               Calling max() and min() on the same list gives both extremes in just two lines of  code.

Python For Computational Problem Solving
 Quick Comparison


max()                     min()

Finds the largest / maximum value                  Finds the smallest / minimum value
Great for scores, prices, rankings                    Great for lowest cost, fastest time



                       Example


       max(10, 20, 5)  →  20
       min(10, 20, 5)  →  5
       max(3.5, 2.1, 9.9)  →  9.9

Python For Computational Problem Solving
Key Takeaways


 •  Both max() and min() are built-in Python functions.

 •  max() returns the largest value.

 •  min() returns the smallest value.

 •  They work with individual values and iterables.

 •  They are useful for basic data analysis and problem solving.

A closure is a nested function which has access to a free variable from an enclosing

•  A generator is a function that returns an iterator that produces a sequence of values
  when iterated over.

•  Iterator - an object that can be iterated upon, i.e. we can traverse through all the values.

•  Generators in Python provides a way to create a function that behaves like an iterator.

•  Does not return a single value; instead, it returns an iterator object with a sequence of
   values.

• A yield statement is used instead of the return statement.

•   If the body of a def contains yield, the function automatically becomes a Python
   generator function.

  produce the values.

•  Python Generator functions return a generator object that is iterable (used as

Pipelining Generators
Multiple generators can be used to pipeline a series of operations

Example: Compute the sum of squares of numbers in the Fibonacci
series
## GeneratorGenerator functionfunction - fibonaccifibonacci_numbersnumbers

    x,y=0,1

# Generator function - square

    for num in nums:
        yield num**2

                It can run multiple times                           It only runs a single time

 function.

Function Generators: Summary

•  Python generator functions allows for the declaration of a function that behaves like an
   iterator, making it a faster, cleaner and easier way to create an iterator.


•  Generators are useful when we want to produce a large sequence of values, but we
   don't want to store all of them in memory at once.


•  The simplification of code is a result of generator function and generator expression
   support provided by Python.

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Introduction to Modules

• A module in Python is simply a file containing Python code,
functions, classes, or variables that you can reuse in other
programs.
• Modules help organize large programs into smaller, manageable,
and reusable pieces.
• Python provides many built-in modules like math, os, random,
and datetime that simplify common programming tasks.
• You can also create your own modules by saving functions in a
.py file and importing them into another program using the import
statement.
• You can also include the third-party modules in the python code.

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Advantages of Modules

Reusability: Write code once and reuse it across multiple programs, reducing duplication and saving development time.
Modularity: Break large programs into smaller, logical parts, making code easier to develop, debug, and maintain.
Separate Namespace: Each module has its own namespace, preventing naming conflicts between functions or variables in different modules.
Better Organization: Groups related functions/classes into structured files and folders, improving project clarity and scalability.

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Types of Modules

Built-in Modules.
User-Defined Modules (Creating your own modules).
PIP - Third Party Modules.

PIP = Pip Installs PackagesTool to install/manage third-party python packages.
Common commands:
pip install package_namepip uninstall package_namepip list

Modules created by the programmerStored as .py files containing functions, classes, or variablesUsed to organize and reuse your own code

Extend Python with advanced or specialized features

Introduction to PIL (Pillow)

What is PIL/Pillow?
Pillow = modern version of Python Imaging Library (PIL)
Used for:
Opening imagesEditing imagesSaving images (multiple formats)

[Image text, OCR]
pillow

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Introduction to PIL (Pillow)

Why use Pillow?
Easy to useSupports many formats (JPEG, PNG, BMP, GIF, TIFF, …)Great for resizing, cropping, rotating, filtering images
Install Pillow
pip install pillow

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Importing & Loading an Image

Load an Image
from PIL import Image
img = Image.open("PES LOGO.jpg")
img.show()

Supported Formats
JPEG, PNG, BMP, GIF, TIFF, and more.

Output:

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Basic Image Information

print(img.format)   # e.g., JPEG
print(img.size)     # (width, height)
print(img.mode)     # RGB, RGBA, L etc.

Meaning
format: file typesize: pixel dimensionsmode: color channels

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Resizing Images

Resizing Images
resized_img = img.resize((200, 200))
resized_img.show()

Note - resize() returns a new image and may distort aspect ratio.
To maintain aspect ratio:
img.thumbnail((200, 200))
img.show()

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Converting Image Modes

Converting Image Modes
gray_img = img.convert("L")
gray_img.show()
Common Modes:
1 → Black & white (1-bit)L → Grayscale (8-bit)RGB → Color (3 channels)RGBA → Color + TransparencyCMYK → Printing format

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Saving, Rotating and Cropping Images

Saving Images
gray_img.save("output_image.png")
 Rotating : rotate(degrees)
rotated_img = img.rotate(45)
rotated_img.show()
Cropping : Image.crop(left, upper, right, lower) pixel coordinates
cropped_img = img.crop((50, 50, 200, 200))
cropped_img.show()

Introduction to re Module

UE25CS151A
Department of Computer Science and Engineering

Prof. Kundhavai K R, CSE Department

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

re Module

The re module in Python provides support for Regular Expressions (regex). Regex is a powerful text-processing tool used to search, match, and manipulate patterns in strings. Helps automate tasks like validation, extraction, text cleaning, and pattern matching. Need not use pip install, as it is a built-in (standard library) module in Python.
A pattern defines what you want to search in text
Examples:
r"\d+" → any sequence of digitsr"\b[Pp]\w+" → words starting with P or pr"\w{3}" → exactly 3 characters
Why not use string methods?
.find() searches exact text
RegEx can match flexible patterns

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Key Metacharacters

Meta | Meaning | Example

. | Any character (except newline) | h.t → hat, hot

\d | Digit (0–9) | \d\d → 12

\w | Word character (a-z, A-Z, 0-9, _) | \w\w → hi, A5

\s | Whitespace | hello\sworld → hello world

+ | One or more | \d+ → 123

* | Zero or more | ab*c → ac, abc

[] | Character set | [aeiou] → any vowel

^ | Start of string | ^Hello

$ | End of string | world$

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Main Functions in re

re.search() → finds first match
re.findall() → finds all matches in a list

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

re.search() Example

import re
text = "My car brand is Audi."
pattern = r"c\w\w"  # 3-letter word starting with 'c'
match = re.search(pattern, text)
if match:
    print(match.group(), match.start(), match.end())
Output:
car 3 6
.group() → actual text.start() → starting index.end() → ending index

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

re.findall() Examples

text = "My numbers: 123, 456, 789."
print(re.findall(r"\d", text))      # single digits → ['1','2',...]
print(re.findall(r"\d+", text))     # full numbers → ['123','456','789']
print(re.findall(r"\w+", "Python is fun!"))  # words → ['Python','is','fun']

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

re.sub() Example

Replace spaces with underscores
import re
text = "Welcome to Python class"
new_text = re.sub(r"\s", "_", text)
print(new_text)

Output:
Welcome_to_Python_class
re.sub(pattern, replacement, text) → substitute function

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Word Boundaries & Quantifiers

\b → word boundary
{n} → exactly n characters
Examples:
text = "The fox ran"
print(re.findall(r"\b\w{3}\b", text))  # ['The','fox','ran']
print(re.findall(r"\w+ing", "learning coding swimming"))  # ['learning','coding','swimming']

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Splitting and Replacing

Splitting

text = "apple, banana orange,grapes"
print(re.split(r"[\s,]+", text))  # split by spaces or commas
Output: ['apple','banana','orange','grapes']

Replacing
text = "Password: 12345"
print(re.sub(r"\d","*",text))  # replace digits → Password: *****

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Matching Patterns

Words starting with p or P:
text = "Python programming is popular"
pattern = r"\b[Pp]\w+"
print(re.findall(pattern, text))  # ['Python','programming','popular']

Text starting with "Hello":
text = "Hello world"
pattern = r"^Hello"
if re.search(pattern, text): print("Starts with Hello")

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Emails & Phone Numbers

Find emails:text = "info@pes.edu, support@pes.com"
print(re.findall(r"\S+@\S+", text))
# ['info@pes.edu','support@pes.com']

Find 10-digit numbers:
text = "Call 9876543210 or 9123456789"
print(re.findall(r"\d{10}", text))

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Emails & Phone Numbers

Find 10-digit numbers starting with 9:
text = "9000000000, 8123456789"
print(re.findall(r"\b9\d{9}\b", text))  # ['9000000000']

     argparse in Python

Command-Line Argument Parsing: Syntax, Workflows & Applications



                        Dr Manjula K
                  Professor, PCPS Anchor 2026 | Department of CSE (AIML)

Python For Computational Problem Solving — UE26CS151A

COURSE OVERVIEW
Agenda & Lecture Roadmap


      Why argparse? — The Case for CLI Parsing
   1   Standard library module, eliminating hardcoded inputs, and automated --help manuals.


      The 4-Step argparse Workflow & Architecture
   2   ArgumentParser container, add_argument(), parse_args(), and Namespace attribute access.


         Positional vs. Optional Arguments
   3   Ordered mandatory parameters vs. flexible - / -- keyword flags with defaults.


         Essential Parameters & Input Validation
   4   Type conversion (int/float), default fallbacks, choices whitelisting, and required flags.


         Practical Applications & Domain Examples
   5    Building student records, CLI calculators, and Machine Learning hyperparameter pipelines.


        Best Practices, Practice Exercises & Summary
   6   Golden rules for CLI tool design, interactive calculator exercises, and core recap.


Python argparse | UE26CS151A | Department of CSE (AIML)                                                                       2

Python For Computational Problem Solving — UE26CS151A

1. INTRODUCTION
What is argparse & Why Use It?


          What is argparse?                   Why is it Useful?

   • Standard Python Library: Built-in module           • Eliminates Hardcoding: Execute the exact
  for processing command-line arguments            same script across multiple datasets and settings
  without third-party installations (no pip install         without altering source code.
   required).
                                                               • Pipeline Automation: Crucial for running
   • Dynamic Runtime Inputs: Allows users to          scripts from bash scripts, cron jobs, Docker
  pass values directly into Python scripts from the        containers, and CI/CD pipelines.
  terminal at launch time.
                                                               • Error Prevention: Enforces required
   • Automated Help Manuals: Automatically         arguments and validates allowed values before
   creates formatted usage guides and option               script execution starts.
  descriptions when invoked with -h or --help.
                                                               • Code Modularity: Cleanly decouples
   • Validation & Type Casting: Converts raw          application algorithms from runtime
   strings into integers, floats, files, and rejects            configuration parameters.
   invalid inputs with clear error messages.
                                                               • Production CLI Design: Follows standard
   • Professional Standard: The standard library     UNIX and Windows command-line
  tool used universally for building clean, user-          conventions for seamless developer interaction.
   friendly CLI utilities.



Python argparse | UE26CS151A | Department of CSE (AIML)                                                                       3

Python For Computational Problem Solving — UE26CS151A

2. CORE WORKFLOW
How argparse Works: Execution Pipeline


     Execution Pipeline Flowchart          Step-by-Step Dataflow

                                                                        •  1. Terminal Invocation: User executes $ python
                                                           app.py --flag value. The operating system shell passes
                                                         arguments to Python via sys.argv.

                                                                        • 2. ArgumentParser Object: Creates the central
                                                                  container: parser =
                                                                argparse.ArgumentParser(description=...). Holds all
                                                       argument metadata.

                                                                        • 3. Argument Registration: parser.add_argument()
                                                                 defines expected flag names, data types, default fallbacks,
                                                                  choices, and help strings.

                                                                        • 4. Parse Command Line: args = parser.parse_args()
                                                                 inspects sys.argv, converts input types, and validates
                                                                    constraints.

                                                                        • 5. Namespace Attribute Access: Values are accessed
                                                                  as clean Python attributes via args.<name> (e.g.
                                                            args.number, args.epochs).

                                                                        • 6. Program Logic: Application logic executes using
                                                                       verified input values. If input is invalid, a formatted error
                                                                                      is displayed immediately.


Python argparse | UE26CS151A | Department of CSE (AIML)                                                                       4

Python For Computational Problem Solving — UE26CS151A

2. CORE WORKFLOW
Basic Syntax & Script Template



          CODE: Standard argparse Template                                             Syntax Component Breakdown

   import argparse                                              • import argparse: Imports Python's built-
                                                                in argument parsing module without external   # Step 1: Create the ArgumentParser object
   parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(                     package dependencies.
       description="Calculate square of a number"
   )                                                              • ArgumentParser(): Initializes the master
                                                           parser container. description= provides a
   # Step 2: Register expected arguments
   parser.add_argument(                                 header summary in --help.
       "number",
       type=int,                                                • add_argument(): Defines an expected
       help="Number to calculate square"                  argument. Takes positional/optional name,
   )                                                    type=, default=, and help= description.

   # Step 3: Parse command-line arguments
   args = parser.parse_args()                                  • parse_args(): Reads command-line tokens
                                                from sys.argv[1:], performs type conversions,
   # Step 4: Access and use parsed values               and builds the args object.
   print("Square =", args.number ** 2)
                                                                  • args.number: Retrieves the parsed value   # Terminal Execution:
   # $ python square.py 5                                       directly using the argument name specified
   # Output: Square = 25                                 during registration.




Python argparse | UE26CS151A | Department of CSE (AIML)                                                                       5

Python For Computational Problem Solving — UE26CS151A

3. ARGUMENT TYPES
Positional Arguments in argparse



          CODE: Positional Argument Example                                        Key Rules: Positional Arguments

   # square_pos.py                                              • Position Determines Meaning: The
   import argparse
                                                        order in which values appear on the
   parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(                 command line determines which parameter
       description="Compute square of integer")             receives the value.

   # Positional argument (no '-' prefix)                     • No Prefix Flags: Positional arguments do
   parser.add_argument(
       "number",                        NOT start with - or -- (e.g. "number",
       type=int,                                                "input_file").
       help="Input integer to be squared"
   )                                                              • Mandatory by Default: If omitted by the
                                                                user, argparse automatically halts execution
   args = parser.parse_args()
   print(f"Square of {args.number} =                      with a missing argument error message.
   {args.number**2}")
                                                                  • Automatic Type Conversion: Setting
   # Execution Cases:                                     type=int ensures strings are safely parsed to
   # $ python square_pos.py 5
                                                               integers before reaching program logic.   # Square of 5 = 25
   #
   # $ python square_pos.py                                    • Best Use Case: Ideal for core required
   # error: the following arguments are required:          inputs that the program cannot operate
         number                                         without (e.g. source filename, target path).


Python argparse | UE26CS151A | Department of CSE (AIML)                                                                       6

Python For Computational Problem Solving — UE26CS151A

3. ARGUMENT TYPES
Optional Arguments & Flags



           CODE: Optional Argument Example                                        Key Rules: Optional Arguments

   # square_opt.py                                              • Hyphen / Dash Prefix: Always prefixed
   import argparse
                                                       with -- (long name) or - (short alias), e.g. --
   parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(                  number or -n.
       description="Compute square with flags")
                                                                  • Order-Independent: Optional flags can
   # Optional argument with '--' and short alias '-       be passed in any order anywhere on the
   n'
   parser.add_argument(                          command line.
       "--number", "-n",
       type=int,                                                • Explicit Clarity: Flag names clearly
       default=2,                                  document what each supplied parameter
       help="Number whose square is required"
                                                          value represents.   )

   args = parser.parse_args()                                  • Default Fallbacks: Can supply default= to
   print("Square =", args.number ** 2)                     define a fallback value when the user omits
                                                          the flag.
   # Execution Cases:
   # 1. Passing flag: $ python square_opt.py --
                                                                  • Forcing Mandatory Flags: An optional   number 5 -> 25
   # 2. Short alias:  $ python square_opt.py -n 7            flag can be made strictly mandatory by adding
   -> 49                                                required=True.
   # 3. Omitted flag: $ python square_opt.py
   -> 4


Python argparse | UE26CS151A | Department of CSE (AIML)                                                                       7

Python For Computational Problem Solving — UE26CS151A

4. PARAMETERS & VALIDATION
Essential add_argument() Parameters


 Parameter      Purpose              Example Syntax             Description & Behavior



 type            Data type conversion       type=int, type=float           Converts raw string input into specified Python
                                                                                        data type automatically.


 default         Fallback value             default=10,                       Supplies default value if argument is omitted
                                            default="app.log"             from command line.


 required       Mandatory flag             required=True                   Forces an optional flag (--name) to be
                                                                             mandatory at runtime.


 choices          Restrict input set           choices=["add", "sub",          Restricts valid input to a specified list; rejects
                                            "mul"]                            other values.


 help           Help documentation        help="Path to input            Text displayed next to argument in auto-
                                            dataset"                         generated --help manual.


 action          Boolean flag control        action="store_true"              Sets attribute to True when flag is present, False
                                                                    when absent.

4. PARAMETERS & VALIDATION
Example: Student Information CLI



                   CODE: student.py                                            Execution Scenarios & Analysis

   import argparse                                                         • Passing All Options: $ python student.py --name
                                                           Ananya --age 20 --course AI
   parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
       description="Display student record details"        -> Name: Ananya | Age: 20 | Course: AI
   )
                                                                                 • Using Default Course: $ python student.py --name
                                                                Rahul --age 19   # Mandatory string and integer options
   parser.add_argument("--name", required=True,
                                                           -> Name: Rahul | Age: 19 | Course: Python (default
                       help="Student full name")
                                                                          applied)

   required=True,                                                          • Missing Required Flag: $ python student.py --name
                       help="Student age in years")        Ananya

   # Optional argument with default fallback               -> error: the following arguments are required: --age
   parser.add_argument("--course",
   default="Python",                                                      • Type Validation Error: $ python student.py --name
                       help="Enrolled course name")        Ananya --age twenty

                                                           -> error: argument --age: invalid int value: 'twenty'   args = parser.parse_args()
   print(f"Name   : {args.name}")                                                                                 • Automatic Protection: The script cleanly catches
   print(f"Age    : {args.age}")                                                                   omissions and invalid types without crashing Python.
   print(f"Course : {args.course}")

   • Self-Documenting CLI: Allows any team                                                --course COURSE  Enrolled course name
  member or user to learn how to operate your                                              (default: Python)

                                              # Notice how required flags and defaults
   • Standard Practice: Always verify your          are clearly

  before sharing.                               user automatically!

Validation with type and choices

   • Automated Help Manuals: Automatically         arguments and validates allowed values before

   • Validation & Type Casting: Converts raw          application algorithms from runtime

2. CORE WORKFLOW
How argparse Works: Execution Pipeline


     Execution Pipeline Flowchart          Step-by-Step Dataflow

                                                                        •  1. Terminal Invocation: User executes $ python
                                                           app.py --flag value. The operating system shell passes
                                                         arguments to Python via sys.argv.

                                                                        • 2. ArgumentParser Object: Creates the central
                                                                  container: parser =
                                                                argparse.ArgumentParser(description=...). Holds all
                                                       argument metadata.

                                                                        • 3. Argument Registration: parser.add_argument()
                                                                 defines expected flag names, data types, default fallbacks,
                                                                  choices, and help strings.

                                                                        • 4. Parse Command Line: args = parser.parse_args()
                                                                 inspects sys.argv, converts input types, and validates
                                                                    constraints.

                                                                        • 5. Namespace Attribute Access: Values are accessed
                                                                  as clean Python attributes via args.<name> (e.g.
                                                            args.number, args.epochs).

                                                                        • 6. Program Logic: Application logic executes using
                                                                       verified input values. If input is invalid, a formatted error
                                                                                      is displayed immediately.

  known as Diamond shaped inheritance

Python For Computational Problem
      Solving- UE26CS151A



          Dr Manjula K
      Professor, PCPS Anchor 2026
      Department of CSE(AIML)

Python For Computational Problem Solving
Why Do We Need Python Environments?


  •  Different projects may require different Python or package
    versions

  •  Virtual environments isolate project dependencies from one
   another

  •  Benefits: avoids conflicts, improves reproducibility, protects
   system Python and simplifies deployment

  • Without isolation, upgrading a package for one project can
    silently break another

Python For Computational Problem Solving
Introduction to Python Environments


   • A Python environment is a workspace where Python and its
    packages are installed and managed for a project

   •  Separate environments help avoid conflicts between package
    versions and project dependencies

   • Key topics covered: virtual environments, venv, pip and
    requirements.txt

   • Used throughout real-world development to keep projects
    reproducible and portable

Python For Computational Problem Solving
What is a Virtual Environment?


  • An isolated directory containing a Python interpreter and a separate
    package installation area

  •  Python provides the built-in venv module for creating virtual
    environments

  • No extra installation needed — venv ships with Python 3.3 and later

  • Each environment behaves like its own self-contained Python installation

Python For Computational Problem Solving
Creating a Virtual Environment


  •  Navigate to the project directory first

  •  Create an environment using venv:

    python -m venv myenv

  •  This creates a folder named myenv containing the interpreter and
   package directories

  • Environment names such as myenv, venv or .venv are common
   conventions

Python For Computational Problem Solving
Activating a Virtual Environment


  • Windows Command Prompt:

    myenv\Scripts\activate

  • Windows PowerShell:

    .\myenv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

  •  Linux / macOS:

    source myenv/bin/activate

  • An active environment is shown by (myenv) in the terminal prompt

Python For Computational Problem Solving
Deactivating a Virtual Environment


   • Use deactivate when finished working with the environment

    deactivate

   •  Deactivation does not delete the environment — it simply exits it

   • The same environment can be reactivated anytime later

Python For Computational Problem Solving
What is pip?


   •  pip is Python’s package installer

   • Used to install, upgrade, remove and inspect Python packages

    python -m pip install numpy

   • Comes bundled with Python by default

   • Works both inside a virtual environment and with the system
   Python

Python For Computational Problem Solving
Installing Packages


  •  Install one package or several packages together

    python -m pip install numpy matplotlib pandas

  •  Packages can be imported into Python right after installation

  •  Installing a specific version:

    python -m pip install numpy==1.26.4

  •  Version constraints using >= and <:

    python -m pip install "numpy>=1.25"  |
    "numpy<2.0"

Python For Computational Problem Solving
Upgrading, Uninstalling & Viewing Packages


    •  Upgrade a package:

     python -m pip install --upgrade numpy

    •  Uninstall a package:

     python -m pip uninstall numpy

    • View installed packages:

     python -m pip list

    •  Package details and dependency list:

     python -m pip show numpy   |   python -m pip
     freeze

Python For Computational Problem Solving
requirements.txt


 •  Contains the exact packages required by a project

 •  Create it:

    python -m pip freeze > requirements.txt

 •  Install everything from it:

    python -m pip install -r requirements.txt

 •  Typical project layout: program.py, requirements.txt,
  README.md

Python For Computational Problem Solving
Sharing a Python Project


  •  Share the project folder along with requirements.txt — not the
   environment itself

  • Another user creates a fresh virtual environment on their own
   machine

  • They install every dependency from requirements.txt in one
   command

  • Keeps projects lightweight, portable and reproducible across
   machines

Python For Computational Problem Solving
Complete Workflow & Example: NumPy Project


  •  Create project → create venv → activate → install packages →
   develop/test → generate requirements.txt → share → recreate
   environment

  • Example: setting up a NumPy project

    mkdir numpy_project

    cd numpy_project

    python -m venv venv

    python -m pip install numpy

Python For Computational Problem Solving

Why Use python -m pip?


  • Runs pip using the specifically selected Python interpreter

  • Reduces confusion when multiple Python installations or
   environments exist

  • Guarantees packages install into the intended environment, not a
    different one

  • Recommended form:

    python -m pip install package_name

Python For Computational Problem Solving
Virtual Environment vs System Python


  • System Python: packages are shared across many projects, so
    conflicts are more likely

  •  Virtual environment: packages are isolated per project,
   minimizing conflicts

Python For Computational Problem Solving
Why Do We Need Python Environments?


  •  Different projects may require different Python or package
    versions

  •  Virtual environments isolate project dependencies from one
   another

  •  Benefits: avoids conflicts, improves reproducibility, protects
   system Python and simplifies deployment

  • Without isolation, upgrading a package for one project can
    silently break another

Python For Computational Problem Solving
Introduction to Python Environments


   • A Python environment is a workspace where Python and its
    packages are installed and managed for a project

   •  Separate environments help avoid conflicts between package
    versions and project dependencies

   • Key topics covered: virtual environments, venv, pip and
    requirements.txt

   • Used throughout real-world development to keep projects
    reproducible and portable

Python For Computational Problem Solving
What is a Virtual Environment?


  • An isolated directory containing a Python interpreter and a separate
    package installation area

  •  Python provides the built-in venv module for creating virtual
    environments

  • No extra installation needed — venv ships with Python 3.3 and later

  • Each environment behaves like its own self-contained Python installation

Python For Computational Problem Solving
Creating a Virtual Environment


  •  Navigate to the project directory first

  •  Create an environment using venv:

    python -m venv myenv

  •  This creates a folder named myenv containing the interpreter and
   package directories

  • Environment names such as myenv, venv or .venv are common
   conventions

Python For Computational Problem Solving
Activating a Virtual Environment


  • Windows Command Prompt:

    myenv\Scripts\activate

  • Windows PowerShell:

    .\myenv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

  •  Linux / macOS:

    source myenv/bin/activate

  • An active environment is shown by (myenv) in the terminal prompt

Python For Computational Problem Solving
Deactivating a Virtual Environment


   • Use deactivate when finished working with the environment

    deactivate

   •  Deactivation does not delete the environment — it simply exits it

   • The same environment can be reactivated anytime later

Python For Computational Problem Solving
What is pip?


   •  pip is Python’s package installer

   • Used to install, upgrade, remove and inspect Python packages

    python -m pip install numpy

   • Comes bundled with Python by default

   • Works both inside a virtual environment and with the system
   Python

Python For Computational Problem Solving
Installing Packages


  •  Install one package or several packages together

    python -m pip install numpy matplotlib pandas

  •  Packages can be imported into Python right after installation

  •  Installing a specific version:

    python -m pip install numpy==1.26.4

  •  Version constraints using >= and <:

    python -m pip install "numpy>=1.25"  |
    "numpy<2.0"

Python For Computational Problem Solving
Upgrading, Uninstalling & Viewing Packages


    •  Upgrade a package:

     python -m pip install --upgrade numpy

    •  Uninstall a package:

     python -m pip uninstall numpy

    • View installed packages:

     python -m pip list

    •  Package details and dependency list:

     python -m pip show numpy   |   python -m pip
     freeze

requirements.txt


 •  Contains the exact packages required by a project

 •  Create it:

    python -m pip freeze > requirements.txt

 •  Install everything from it:

    python -m pip install -r requirements.txt

 •  Typical project layout: program.py, requirements.txt,
  README.md

Sharing a Python Project


  •  Share the project folder along with requirements.txt — not the
   environment itself

  • Another user creates a fresh virtual environment on their own
   machine

  • They install every dependency from requirements.txt in one
   command

  • Keeps projects lightweight, portable and reproducible across
   machines

  •  Create project → create venv → activate → install packages →

Introduction

•  Polymorphism refers to having multiple forms.

•   refersf   to the use off the same ffunction name, but with differentff      signatures

•   allows objects of different classes to be treated as objects of a common
   superclass.

•   This concept enables a single interface to be used for entities of different types.

 Polymorphism

Runtime Polymorphism
•   Python supports runtime polymorphism by using techniques  like method
   overloading and method overriding

••   RuntimeRuntime polymorphismpolymorphism  isis thethe abilityability ofof anan objectobject toto behavebehave differentlydifferently basedbased
   on its actual type during program execution

•    It is also known as dynamic polymorphism

•    It enables the same method name to behave differently based on
   the specific class instance at runtime.



                                                                                                                                          3

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
 Polymorphism

Key Aspects of Runtime Polymorphism:
1.Inheritance:
    •  Runtime polymorphism is closely associated with inheritance.

    •  Subclasses  inherit methods from  their  superclass, and they can
      provided  theirh  own implementationl                ffor theseh   methods.h d

2.Method Overriding:
    •  Subclasses override methods from their superclass to provide their
     own specialized implementation.

    •  The method signature remains the same in both the superclass and
       subclass.
                                                                                                                                          4

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Polymorphism

3.Dynamic Binding:

•  During runtime, the appropriate method to execute is dynamically determined

•    It is based on the actual type of the object invoking the method


4.Common Interface:

•   Different subclasses sharing a common superclass interface

•   Exhibits different behaviors based on their  specific implementations.


                                                                                                                                          5

Polymorphism

runtime polymorphism.

method from the ‘shape’ superclass to provide their specific area calculation.

The method ‘calculate_area’ is called on objects of different types(‘rect’ or ‘circle’) .
The appropriate overridden method is executed based on the object’s actual type.

This happens at the runtime and method execution is dynamically bound to the
object’s specific implementation.

Polymorphism

     self.radius = radius

  def calculate_area(self):
    return 3.14 ** self.radiuslf  d   ** self.radiuslf  d

Introduction

An  iterator  is an object that allows iteration through a sequence of

__next__().

 __iter__()::iter   ():: returnsreturns thethe iteratoriterator objectobject itselfitself andand isis calledcalled whenwhen thethe iteratoriterator
is initialized.

__next__():: returns the next item in the sequence.

When there are no more elements to return, it raises the StopIteration
exception.

 Introduction


Iterators lazy object or Eager object?


Lazyy Evaluation: Iterators follow the principlep   p   of lazyy evaluation,, meaningg
they generate values on-demand rather than computing all values at once.


This can be memory-efficient when dealing with large datasets as it only
retrieves elements as needed.



                                                                                                                                          3
